overview: Spicy's NoClip is a wall-phase module ported from Sigma 2's Phase (the file's NOTICE comment names the gitlab source). Enabling nudges the player up by 0.0784001 blocks, the classic step-over epsilon. Every pre-motion tick, when the player is collided horizontally and not on a ladder, the module computes a movement-input vector scaled by 0.4 and rotated by the yaw, sends a C04PacketPlayerPosition for the horizontal nudge and a second C04PacketPlayerPosition lifting the reported y by 3.0, both with onGround false and both through the fork's sendPacketNoEvent path so the outgoing event bus never re-captures them, then sets the local position to the nudged spot. A bounding-box sweep helper, isInsideBlock, scans the colliding blocks with a full-box override for hoppers, but no handler calls it in this snapshot.

sections.p: The handler fires on EventMotion pre. It builds mx and mz from the yaw plus 90 degrees, mixes the forward and strafe inputs at the 0.4 scale, and, gated on isCollidedHorizontally and not on a ladder, sends the pair: C04PacketPlayerPosition(posX + x, posY, posZ + z, false) followed by C04PacketPlayerPosition(posX, posY + 3.0, posZ, false). The horizontal packet carries the player through the wall face it is pressed against, the vertical packet rides the 3-block climb the phase needs, and the local setPosition snaps the client to the nudged coordinates so the next tick's collision state reflects the new spot. Both packets travel with onGround false.

sendPacketNoEvent is the fork's silent send: it flushes the outbound queue and dispatches the packet straight to the channel without firing the outgoing event bus that Spicy's own modules listen on. That silence keeps the module's traffic invisible to sibling modules such as the Bhop lagback guard and the Disabler, which hook the event stream rather than the raw channel. The 0.0784001 on-enable nudge is the same epsilon the client's step handling uses, and it positions the player just above the floor so the first phase tick has clean collision state.

isInsideBlock is a full box sweep: it iterates the cells overlapped by the bounding box, collects each block's collision box, substitutes a full cube for hoppers (whose real collision box is a thin funnel), and reports whether the player intersects any solid box. It is the classic phase detector and it is never called, so the module does not know whether it is inside a block; it phases purely on the horizontal-collision flag. The Sigma lineage shows in the structure: the same yaw-rotated 0.4 vector, the 3.0 lift and the on-enable epsilon appear in the original Phase.

files.label: NoClip.java (module)
files.explanation:
The module is one EventMotion handler plus the dead isInsideBlock helper. onEnable lifts the player 0.0784001 blocks, onDisable does nothing, and the event branch runs the phase pair whenever the horizontal-collision gate opens. The C04 constructors are the packet-position subtype of C03PacketPlayer, so every phase produces two movement packets with positions but no rotation, both claiming onGround false.

The unused isInsideBlock sweep and the unused MovementUtils import are the port's leftovers: the Sigma original used the box test to decide when to phase, while this port phases on isCollidedHorizontally alone and never checks what it is colliding with. The hopper override is the one interesting relic, since hoppers expose a funnel-shaped hitbox and a naive box test would miss a player standing in the funnel.

files.label: NetworkManager.java (silent send)
files.explanation:
The fork's NetworkManager adds sendPacketNoEvent next to the vanilla sendPacket family: it flushes the outbound queue and dispatches the packet with a null listener, bypassing the Spicy event bus that normal sends traverse. NoClip calls it on the getNetHandler().getNetworkManager() instance, which is why the phase pair never loops back into the module's own or any sibling module's outgoing-packet handlers.

The channel-open guard mirrors the vanilla behavior: while the channel is open the packet is dispatched immediately, otherwise it is queued in outboundPacketsQueue for the next flush. The method is shared by every Spicy module that wants silent traffic, from the combat modules' silent attacks to the player Disabler's injected packets.

countering.label: Passable (swept-box transit)
countering.explanation:
NCP's Passable check performs a swept-box ray trace between the reported from and to positions, retrying along the axes when the first pass collides, and it is constructed with setIgnoreInitiallyColliding(true): a player resting inside a block is not flagged, the transit into the block is. The check measures the movement path itself, so a teleport that crosses solid geometry flags even when both endpoints look legal.

The phase pair is exactly a transit. The horizontal C04 carries the reported position into the wall face the player is pressed against, and the swept box from the pre-move spot to the nudged spot crosses the solid cell, which is the violation. The 3.0 lift adds a vertical sweep that crosses the ceiling blocks above a phasing player. The ignore-initially-colliding flag is what makes the check accurate here: it does not punish the player for standing in a wall, it punishes the move that entered it.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly's vertical allowance, vDistRel, seeds from the previous move's momentum and accepts only named envelopes: zero-y on ground, jump, step-up, riptide. The horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation's sprint prediction, and ground state is ray-traced from the block cache, never the packet flag. A violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) plus max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) times 100 with a set-back.

The 3.0 vertical packet is the first thing the envelope sees: a 3-block climb is not a jump (0.42), not a step-up (capped by sfStepHeight, default 0.6), and carries no momentum seed, so yDistanceAboveLimit lands near 2.4 and the violation is in the hundreds on the first phase. The horizontal nudge, repeated every tick a wall is hugged, exceeds the sprint prediction by the 0.4-scale vector, so the phase stream accumulates horizontal violations on top.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation:
MorePackets counts serverbound move packets against a window ceiling of 22 per second with 20 ideal, scored in 500ms buckets, with a burst path on the newest half-second bucket (15 packets default, direct violation at 10). The check is invoked from MovingListener on every processed move, so the phase pair counts as two moves per tick.

Wall-hugging phases sustain the pair every tick: 2 extra C04s on top of the regular move, roughly 60 packets per second while the player phases along a wall, which is nearly three times the window ceiling and well past the burst path's 15-per-half-second limit. The burst path is the one that matters for short phase episodes, and the window accumulator takes over when the player phases for several seconds. Content-blind as it is, the check cannot be confused by the onGround false claims.

countering.label: Phase (swept-AABB collision)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Phase check runs a tesseract swept-AABB from the previous position to the reported position against the solid collision boxes, and on any intersection punishes the player and tries to rubberband them back. The distance guard skips moves whose squared distance exceeds 65, which is why the y+120 and y+11 teleports of classic vertical phase modes escape it.

The module's pair is inside the checked envelope: the horizontal nudge's squared distance is at most about 0.32 (0.4 scale, mixed inputs), and the 3.0 lift contributes 9, so both packets are swept and both cross solid geometry when the player is pressed into a wall, producing the violation and the rubberband. The on-enable 0.0784001 nudge is sub-threshold on its own. The honest gap is the classic one: a phase that teleports the player 9 or more blocks in one move (squared distance over 65) skips the swept test entirely, though the vertical envelope checks still see it.
